absent: Numeric encodings and bit positions for hypercall numbers, GHCB MSR fields, exit codes, and error selectors.
Complete GHCB and PSC descriptor layouts beyond the header and control fields touched here.
Firmware behavior for SNP guest request commands and staging buffer ownership outside the guarded section.
Implementations of referenced but unrouted helpers for guest memory access, scratch setup, VMSA reload internals, and PSC and MMIO completion.
Lock ordering and sleep context constraints for the SNP save area and guest request mutexes relative to other KVM locks.
Userspace protocols for mapping hypercalls and certificate provisioning beyond the request address length and status fields shown.
Validation details for APIC identity lookup, address translatability checks, and jump table lifecycle.

findings.text: Reload helper for SNP virtual machine save area state exposed to other compilation units. It serializes against concurrent AP lifecycle updates and refreshes the loaded save area from the remembered guest address.
Top level handler for secure guest exit events. It accepts a virtual CPU context and reports whether control returns promptly to the guest, leaves to userspace, or signals an error.
Shared dispatcher for SVM exit reasons. It validates the numeric reason, applies speculative index hardening, and invokes the registered handler or the unexpected exit path.
Emulation helper that advances past the triggering instruction and then places the virtual CPU into the AP reset hold quiescent condition.

Memory mapped input output emulation entry for encrypted guests with a scratch buffer. It consumes whole transfer lengths synchronously when possible and otherwise queues a single fragment for userspace completion.
Header helper that records a pending virtual CPU request and then wakes the target, propagating the wait attribute carried in the request identifier.
Guest exit dispatch first distinguishes MSR protocol use by informational bits in the control address, then treats a zero address or a mapping failure as a benign resume without guest visible error.

SNP guests must present a previously registered control address, must use usage zero, must provide required input fields, and SNP only event types are rejected for non SNP guests with dedicated guest visible error indications.

Page state change startup requires userspace opt in for the mapping hypercall, derives an entry bound from scratch length, and rejects an out of range end index with header error completion rather than entering the scan.

Application processor creation validates target identity, feature compatibility, and address acceptability, refuses two megabyte aligned save area addresses as unsafe, and treats unknown operation selectors as invalid.

Basic and extended guest requests require SNP membership, page aligned and distinct request and response addresses, and valid address registers for report data, with malformed inputs receiving a generic invalid input indication and guest resume.

Report type extended requests consult a per virtual machine certificates enablement flag. When enabled they leave to userspace with address and length, otherwise an empty certificate terminator may be cleared in guest memory before direct firmware handling.

Several MSR protocol operations are SNP only and otherwise terminate to userspace as a system event. Termination requests and explicit preference registration and feature query operations produce architected response encodings.
Emulated secure MMIO requires non empty length, caps GHCB version two transfers at eight bytes, and prepares scratch state before delegating to the generic secure MMIO path.

SVM dispatch treats high bit failure indications from run as unexpected exits except under hypervisor, honors dedicated fast paths under retpoline mitigation, and bounds table lookup before invocation.
The per virtual CPU SNP save area mutex serializes reload of the loaded save area against application processor creation and destruction updates to pending address and waiting state.
The per virtual machine guest request mutex serializes access to shared request and response staging buffers across concurrent SNP guest request handling on different virtual CPUs.

Per virtual CPU secure state retains scratch area location and length, mapped control block address, registered control address, current and end page state indices, pending and loaded save area addresses, reset hold classification, and waiting for reset indication.

Host userspace communication uses a hypercall area carrying number return and address length and attribute arguments, a certificate request area carrying address length and status, a system event area carrying type count and payload, and a single entry MMIO fragment queue with completion callback.

Secure exit handling uses a tri state result where zero means leave to userspace with a completion routine armed, one means resume the guest, and negative means host error. Success and error indications are also reflected into guest visible control state.

Private versus shared page conversion is forwarded to userspace as a mapping hypercall with cleared return for compatibility, page size attribute, and a page state completion callback. Ranges containing only unsupported operations complete internally without leaving to userspace.

Valid creation stores a pending save area address while destruction stores an invalid marker, both set a waiting for reset flag and, except for deferred creation until initial signal, request protected state update and wake the target.

Certificate provisioning maps userspace status to guest behavior with success re entering firmware handling, insufficient space reporting length with invalid length error, temporary unavailability reporting busy, input output failure reporting generic error, and other statuses as host errors.

Halt emulation counts the exit, then either updates multiprocessor state in kernel with runnable override on pending events or paravirtual unhalt, or leaves to userspace with the supplied reason when the local interrupt controller is emulated outside the kernel.

MSR protocol entry serves information, identifier, reset hold, hypervisor feature, preferred address, address registration, page state, and termination operations, preserving the incoming value on unknown or failed identifier handling.

Memory based exits for common operations such as input output, debug, time, identifier, cache control, and call are re dispatched through the shared SVM exit dispatcher after initial secure validation and success marking.
The guest owned page state descriptor can change after validation, so only one time read copies of current and end indices are used for bounds checks and traversal.
A guest supplied save area address that is large page aligned is rejected because hostile large page manipulation could trigger incorrect fault signaling under a hardware erratum.
Secure MMIO emulation rejects absent data pointers and pointers that reside on the host stack, avoiding lifetime and aliasing hazards during synchronous and userspace completed transfers.
Firmware reported failures for guest requests are conveyed to the guest without host action, while transport failures without firmware status are propagated to userspace as host errors.

Page conversion forwarding uses hypercall number KVM_HC_MAP_GPA_RANGE with attribute selectors KVM_MAP_GPA_RANGE_DECRYPTED and KVM_MAP_GPA_RANGE_ENCRYPTED and size selectors KVM_MAP_GPA_RANGE_PAGE_SZ_4K and KVM_MAP_GPA_RANGE_PAGE_SZ_2M.

Secure dispatch distinguishes selectors SVM_VMGEXIT_PSC and SVM_VMGEXIT_EXT_GUEST_REQUEST and SVM_VMGEXIT_GUEST_REQUEST and SVM_VMGEXIT_AP_CREATION as SNP only, with guest indications GHCB_ERR_INVALID_INPUT and GHCB_ERR_INVALID_EVENT and GHCB_ERR_MISSING_INPUT and GHCB_ERR_NOT_REGISTERED and certificate errors SNP_GUEST_VMM_ERR_INVALID_LEN and SNP_GUEST_VMM_ERR_BUSY and SNP_GUEST_VMM_ERR_GENERIC.

Host control uses exit reasons KVM_EXIT_SYSTEM_EVENT and KVM_EXIT_SNP_REQ_CERTS and KVM_EXIT_AP_RESET_HOLD with system type KVM_SYSTEM_EVENT_SEV_TERM, processor states KVM_MP_STATE_RUNNABLE and KVM_MP_STATE_AP_RESET_HOLD, and request identifiers KVM_REQ_EVENT and KVM_REQ_UPDATE_PROTECTED_GUEST_STATE.

MSR protocol distinguishes request selectors GHCB_MSR_TERM_REQ and GHCB_MSR_PSC_REQ and GHCB_MSR_REG_GPA_REQ and GHCB_MSR_PREF_GPA_REQ and GHCB_MSR_HV_FT_REQ and GHCB_MSR_AP_RESET_HOLD_REQ and GHCB_MSR_CPUID_REQ and GHCB_MSR_SEV_INFO_REQ with corresponding response selectors.
